chapter_title: Concerning these Names: God, Rich One, and Angel;

3.original: [in the land of light, and there is no measure to]
3.content: in the land of light, and there is no measure to

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Three Archetypes

**¶1:** To this reality a quality is attributed in the natural mind. For people confess it outwardly with their speech: "Divine good," "abundance of truth," and "receptive form of wisdom." But what are these in themselves? What is Divine good in its essence? What is the abundance of truth? What is the receptive form of wisdom? What are these [GAP-1: three degrees of spiritual proceeding]?

**¶3:** These three degrees of spiritual proceeding exist [GAP-2: in the realm of Divine wisdom, and there is no limit to] them.

**¶4:** Those realities called "Divine good" are the goods that the Divine Love brought forth from Itself. He established them according to the form of His own infinite goodness.

**¶5:** Conversely, those that are named "abundances of truth [GAP-3: derived from good]" are the derivative states proceeding from the first goods of Divine Love; because when the Divine Love had brought forth the primary goods, those goods themselves brought forth derivative states of truth. These are called "abundances."

**¶6:** These abundances of truth, in turn, brought forth their own derivative states, which are called "receptive forms of wisdom." These are the three degrees of proceeding that exist in the realm of Divine wisdom. They are infinite and cannot be delimited.

**¶7:** Other realities called "Divine good" are the emanations that have come forth from the Divine Love — the goods that He brought forth and sent out into spiritual combat, where they overcame the opposition of evil and falsity.

**¶8:** Conversely, the "abundances of truth" are derivative states proceeding from those first living Divine truths. These abundances of truth have likewise come forth and accomplished and fulfilled the purpose of the Divine, in both the interior and the exterior states of life.

**¶9:** And those called "receptive forms of wisdom" are the derivative truths proceeding from the abundances, which had come forth from the three living Divine truths. They have been sent as a mission and an apostolate into this constructed spiritual order. They have come to all that is Divine within the soul which dwells in stillness and in concealment — that is, to the inmost good not yet made manifest. And they have also come to all the affections that have been entangled in evil. They have brought to those affections hope and trust.

**¶10:** Again, "Divine good" is the name given to all the goods belonging to the province of the Divine Proceeding as Life.

**¶11:** Conversely, "receptive forms of wisdom" is the name given to all the truths that receive and transmit, belonging to the province of the Lord as the Beloved of all wisdoms.

**¶12:** And "abundances of truth" is the name given to all the knowledges belonging to the province of the glorious Mediating Presence — the Lord as He stands between the Divine itself and the recipient forms below, communicating the fullness of truth into every degree of the spiritual order.

---

*Note on structure:* The teaching unfolds one doctrine through three applications — first as an eternal reality within the Divine wisdom itself (¶3–6), then as an active proceeding into spiritual combat and redemption (¶7–9), and finally as a living arrangement within the heavenly kingdom under three governing principles (¶10–12). This maps precisely to what Swedenborg calls the celestial, spiritual, and natural degrees of a single Divine proceeding — good begetting truth, truth begetting receptive forms, each degree infinite in itself.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: This one, a name is given to him in the world. For people pronounce it with their mouths: 'god', 'rich one', and 'angel'. Who are they? Who are the gods? Or who are the rich ones? Or who are the angels? Who are these [three] archetypes?
There are these three archetypes [in the land of light, and there is no measure to] them!
So, the ones who are called 'god', are the gods whom the Father has summoned from himself. He has established them after the likeness of his greatness.

Conversely, these who are named 'rich [ones]', are the evocations of the first rich gods of the Father; because, when the Father had summoned (the first), they themselves summoned evocations. They called them 'rich'.
They too, the rich ones, have summoned their evocations. They call them 'angel'. These are the three archetypes who occur in the land of light. There is no measure to apply to them!
Other persons who are named 'god' are the emanations who have come from the Father; the evocations of the Father whom he summoned forth. They came out to the contest and humiliated the enmity.

Conversely, the 'rich ones' are the evocations of these first living words. They too, the rich ones, have come and performed and fulfilled the pleasure of the greatness, in the worlds that are above and below.

On the other hand, the ones who are named the 'angels' are the evocations of the rich ones, who had come from the three living words. They have been sent in an embassy and an apostolate to this building. They have come to the entire divinity, which is established in silence and in hiddenness. And, also, they have come to all the souls who have been entangled in the enemy. They have brought them hope and confidence.
Again, they are called 'god', all the gods who belong to the household of the Great Spirit.
Conversely, the ones who are called 'angel', are all the angels who belong to the household of the Beloved of the Lights.
The ones who are called 'rich', are all the rich ones who belong to the household of the glorious Ambassador.

fills.explanation: The text explicitly names three titles (god, rich one, angel), and ¶3 and ¶6 both confirm "three archetypes"; the spiritual reading likewise says "three degrees of spiritual proceeding," so the editor's word is correct.

fills.explanation: The closing summary in ¶6 restates this exact formula verbatim — "These are the three archetypes who occur in the land of light. There is no measure to apply to them!" — confirming the editor's reconstruction precisely.

The standard designation throughout the chapter is "rich ones" (see ¶1, ¶3, ¶6, ¶8, ¶12), and the spiritual reading's "derived from good" describes the spiritual meaning of the term rather than requiring additional natural-plane words beyond completing the stock epithet.
